subject: physics
title: Waves Adventure 1: Wave properties and v = fλ
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet transverse and longitudinal waves and use v = fλ.
meta_desc: Physics — wave types, transverse vs longitudinal, frequency, wavelength, v = fλ.
final_note: You learned waves transfer energy without matter, transverse waves oscillate ⊥ to motion (light, water), longitudinal ∥ (sound), and v = fλ.

concepts.def: Vibrations perpendicular (light) or parallel (sound) to travel.
Number of waves per second and the length of one wave.
v = f × λ, the speed a wave travels.
Maximum displacement from the rest position; relates to energy.
Radio to gamma; all travel at the speed of light in a vacuum.
Waves bounce off surfaces or change direction when changing medium.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Transverse: oscillation ⊥ direction of travel. Examples: water surface, EM waves (light, radio), seismic S-waves.

Longitudinal: oscillation parallel. Examples: sound, seismic P-waves. Compressions and rarefactions.

v = f · λ

f in Hz (1/s), λ in m, v in m/s.

Sound in air: v ≈ 340 m/s.
Light in vacuum: c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s.

Period T = 1/f.

Wavefronts: lines of equal phase (e.g. crests).
Rays: arrows perpendicular to wavefronts, showing direction.

Reflection: angle in = angle out.
Refraction: v changes → λ changes (f unchanged); ray bends.
Snell: n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂.

mcqs.q: Why does a metal spoon in hot water heat up faster than a wooden one?
options: Yes — but only after billions of years on Earth's scale.
Metals have higher thermal conductivity, so heat is transferred more rapidly through them.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Metal heats up faster because it has a lower specific heat capacity, requiring less energy per degree.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between heat and temperature?
options: Heat is the energy transferred due to temperature difference; temperature measures average kinetic energy of particles.
Metal heats up faster because it has more thermal energy to begin with.
Heat and temperature are the same thing — both measure how hot something is.
Heat is measured in degrees Celsius and temperature in Joules.
